Moderator: Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the CDSL Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference 
Call, hosted by HDFC Securities. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in listen-only mode 
and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should 
you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star, then 
zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
Ladies and gentlemen, please note that CDSL does not provide specific revenue or earnings 
guidance. Anything said on this call, which reflects CDSL's outlook for the future or which could 
be constituted as forward-looking statements must be reviewed in conjunction with the risks that 
the company faces. 
I would now like to hand the conference over to Mr. Amit Chandra from HDFC Securities. 
Thank you, and over to you. 
Amit Chandra: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone. On behalf of HDFC Securities, we welcome 
you all to the CDSL quarter 2 FY27 earnings call. Today, we have with us the management team 
of CDSL, represented by Mr. Nehal Vora, MD and CEO; Mr. Girish Amesara, CFO; and other 
senior leaders from the management team. 
We will start with a brief overview of the quarter by Mr. Nehal Vora, and then we'll open up the 
floor for the question-and-answer session. Thank you, and over to you, Nehal, sir. 
Nehal Vora: So first of all, thank you, Amit. A very good afternoon and a warm welcome to everyone joining 
us today. I hope each of you and your loved ones are safe and healthy. Thank you for joining us 
to discuss CDSL's financial results for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026. A detailed 
investor presentation has been uploaded on our website for your reference. 
I'm joined today by the leadership team of the CDSL Group. Let me begin by briefly sharing the 
broader market context and some of the key developments during the quarter before the CFO 
takes us through the financial performance in greater detail. 
During the quarter, Indian securities market saw continued activity, particularly in the primary 
market, even up against a more volatile broader market environment, led by geopolitical issues. 
IPO proceeds exceeded US$9 billion or INR86,500 crores in the July to September quarter, 
highest ever for this period. September which has seen about 34 IPOs, the highest in a single 
month since December '96. 
Demat accounts additions also remain significant. The industry added approximately 32.7 lakh 
accounts in August, the highest monthly addition in 7 months. By the end of September, the 
overall Demat account base has reached approximately 24 crores. CDSL continued to account 
for approximately 80%+of the industry's demat accounts with about 19.34 crores accounts by 
the end of September 2026. We shall shortly be publishing the number of demat accounts for 
October end on our website. 
The IPO surge growth in demat accounts and the other market developments underline the 
importance of building capacity ahead of needs. Our continuing investments in technology and 
people are aimed at ensuring that CDSL remains resilient and equipped to support the evolving

Central Depository Services (India) Limited 
 November 02, 2026 
Page 3 of 10

scale of the India securities markets while maintaining the dependable service and helping 
investors navigate both favourable and challenging market conditions. 
Further to the appointments of our Executive Directors on CDSL during the last quarter, we have 
also continued to strengthen our leadership across two important functions in this quarter. Shri 
Farokh Patel has been elevated to the role of Chief Regulatory Officer and Compliance Officer 
of the company with effect from September 1, 2026. We've also welcomed Shri Kinjal Shah as 
our Chief Technology Officer with effect from September 22, 2026. We welcome them to their 
respective roles and look forward to their contribution. 
Also, additionally, a significant and important initiative, in which RBI has enabled depositories 
to include information on bank deposits in the consolidated account statement through the 
account aggregator system, is a step towards providing investors with a more comprehensive 
view of the financial assets in one place. 
On the Investor Education and Protection Fund, CDSL continues on its efforts towards further 
strengthening investor education. As a part of the World Investor Week 2026 and Project 
Jagrook's campaign theme of “Samajh Se Investing Simple”, CDSL IPF organized an 
experience-based learning investor awareness initiative aimed at investors of different 
demographic groups across India. Its 50 cycle rallies across 12 states and over 45 districts 
reached around 10,000 participants. 
Our partnership with Amar Chitra Katha is gaining popularity. And to sustain its momentum, 
we also launched the “Garden of Prosperity” in 12 languages with Amar Chitra Katha and 
distributed investor education comics to nearly 30,000-plus students across 60 schools. I would 
really encourage all of you to look at all this on the CDSL IPF website for you and your families. 
As part of the Reimagine symposium, the registrations are now open for the second edition of a 
Reimagine Ideathon, inviting students to propose practical ideas around financial awareness and 
cyber safety. I would especially request the investors listening today to encourage the young 
people in as per your families and other known people to participate in this. Building a more 
informed and secure market will also require us to look at and see what the next generation 
expects us to do to shape its future. 
The CFO will take you through the financial results for the quarter and half year. The earnings 
call presentation has been also put out on basically the stock exchange website, and it's available 
on the CDSL website, which provides a detailed breakdown of revenue and expenses in the last 
five quarters, along with the necessary information. 
The markets will continue to move through periods of optimism as well as certain amounts of 
issues which are happening on the geopolitical front. But what matters to CDSL and to the wider 
ecosystem is the strength of the foundation behind them. For institutions like us, that means 
continuing to build infrastructure at a secure, resilient and continue and be trusted by millions 
of investors is what our core focus remains. 
Our priorities remain unchanged, strengthen the core, prepare for the future through initiatives 
like various initiatives, which basically with SEBI and other parts of the ecosystem continue to

Central Depository Services (India) Limited 
 November 02, 2026 
Page 4 of 10

do for us. And also invest a lot of time and energy in the investment education initiatives to truly 
making investors truly self-sufficient. 
We remain grateful to our regulators, SEBI, RBI and the Ministry of Finance and to our 
depository participants, issuers, investors, market intermediaries, shareholders and employees 
for their continued support and trust. 
With that, I now hand it over to the CFO to take us through the financial performance in great 
detail. Thank you, and Jai Hind. 
Girish Amesara: Thank you, Nehal. Good afternoon, everyone. I will start with the standalone. For the 6 months 
ended September 30, 2026, the total income is achieved at INR685.21 crores as against 
INR602.26 crores for the 6 months of the previous year. The standalone net profit for the 6 
months, is achieved at INR307.79 crores as against INR279.51 crores for the first half of the 
previous year. 
In terms of quarterly numbers, the stand-alone total income is at INR358.70 crores as against 
INR289.90 crores for the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The standalone net profit 
for second quarter is INR163.34 crores as against INR127.50 crores for the corresponding 
quarter of the previous year. 
On a consolidated total income for 6 months ended 30th September 2026 is achieved at 
INR757.80 crores as against INR636.53 crores of the first half of the previous year. The 
consolidated net profit for the 6 months ended September 30th is at INR290.97 crores as against 
INR242.34 crores for the previous year. 
For the second quarter on a consolidated basis, the total income is achieved at INR417.30 crores, 
which is against INR341.57 crores for the corresponding quarter of the previous year. And the 
net profit for second quarter is at INR173.30 crores as against INR139.93 crores of the 
corresponding quarter in the previous year. 
The other income in stand-alone financial results include dividend received from a subsidiary 
company amounting to INR39.50 crores, which was received in June quarter as compared to 
INR62 crores received in a similar quarter during the previous year. 
The dividend is eliminated on consolidation as that is received from a subsidiary company. If 
we consider the standalone profitability without considering the subsidiary dividend, the net 
profit for 6 months on a stand-alone basis is at INR268.29 crores as against INR217.51 crores 
for the corresponding first half of the previous year. 
With this, I will request Sunil to take us through CVL numbers. Thank you, and over to you to 
Sunil. 
Sunil Alvares: Thank you, Girish. Good afternoon, everyone, and I'm presenting before you the H1 FY27 
results for CVL. During H1 FY27, revenue grew by 20% to INR99.91 crores, as compared to 
INR83.52 crores in the previous year. Other income declined by 16% to INR7.82 crores from 
INR9.31 crores in the corresponding period.

Consequently, the total income increased by 16% to INR107.70 crores compared to INR92.84 
crores in the previous year. Total expenditure increased by 33% to INR75.81 crores compared 
to INR57.01 crores in H1 FY26. Profit before tax moderated by 11% to INR21.91 crores from 
INR35.83 crores in H1 FY26. Profit after tax for H1 FY27 stood at INR23.74 crores compared 
to INR27.09 crores in H1 '26, representing a decline of 12%. 
With this, I'll open the floor for questions and answers. 
Moderator: Thank you very much. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. We'll take the first 
question from the line of Amit Chandra from HDFC Securities. 
Amit Chandra: Congrats for a very strong set of numbers. Sir, my first question is, we are seeing very strong 
recovery in this quarter. And thanks to the IPO, the revenue in this quarter and the recovery in 
the online data charges. So just to understand if there is any kind of one-off in the IPO, or is it 
purely driven by the higher number of IPOs? And also, if you can provide some color in terms 
of what could be the steady-state IPO revenues that we can assume or the mix between IPO and 
the corporate action? 
And on the online data, obviously, there has been a recovery. We had the pricing impact. So is 
it safe to assume that this is a new base and the pricing impact is behind? And also here, the 
growth of 20% Q-o-Q is slightly lower than the 30% growth that we have seen in the incremental 
BO accounts. So, has there been any change in terms of fetch versus the newer accounts opening 
charges that we have in the online data? 
Nehal Vora: So, on the first one, Amit, I think it's the number of IPOs which have come in, and I think looking 
at what terms of the prospectuses, which have been filed with SEBI, we hope that this trend 
continues. It's not specific to any particular IPO or a one-off. It's a general uptick on the number 
of IPOs, which are hitting the market and probably may be expected to hit. But again, that's a 
forward-looking statement. So, we will not be able to comment on that. 
The important point, which I would like to make here is that we continue to invest in our 
infrastructure that as the surge happens, and these were a series of questions in the past calls that 
why we are investing in technology. It's times like these where we see really the dividend where 
the number of activity goes up, CDSL is able to manage that kind of load, and we'll continue to 
embark on this journey to invest in technology as well as the employees. On the second point, 
I'll ask Sunil to answer on the online charges. 
Sunil Alvares: The, the online charges, we have seen a higher number of records created and which have been 
fetched. To, to a large extent, it has taken care of the pricing impact, which was which was 
introduced from 1st April 2026. I hope that answers your question. 
Amit Chandra: Okay. So, any significant change that has happened in the mix of fetch versus create within 
online? And what would be the blended pricing after the pricing change? 
Sunil Alvares: After the pricing change, see for creation, it has come down to INR5. And for fetching it has 
come down to INR28. So, for creation, it was reduced by 75% and for fetch, it was reduced by 
20%.

Amit Chandra: Okay. And sir, on the expenses part, obviously, there has been a margin expansion because of 
the top line growth. But if I see the technology expenses, in the last call, you have said that most 
of the technological investments are mostly behind. 
In terms of the like the major upgrades are behind and maybe the incremental growth in 
technology would be a bit like moderate or on a steady-state basis. So but still the Y-o-Y growth 
is still at 38%, 39%. 
So how do you see this in terms of obviously, you said that you have been investing in 
technology, but the pace of the investment is still the same? Or are the major bulk of the 
investments are behind us? 
Nehal Vora: So again, I don't think I mentioned that, what I had mentioned, I clearly remember is that we 
continue to invest in technology because technology is something which continues to evolve. 
The market conditions continue to evolve. 
We've seen some record IPOs hitting the market, and it has been due to the effort of the team 
and the system planning, which has happened, it has gone seamlessly well. So, we continue to 
embark on this journey. I don't think we can really sit assured that our technology systems are 
fine because there are a lot of innovations which happen, better way of doing things. 
The market environment is changing very quickly. So, we continue to have the ear on the ground 
and wherever it's required, we continue to invest so that the efficiency improves, the client 
experience improves. And as more and more people are enticed into hitting markets, we are 
completely well prepared in terms of going forward. 
So, I don't think we should and anyway, we don't comment on the future. But the principle 
remains the same that we continue to embark on this journey to ensure that the robustness and 
the resiliency of the CDSL system remains top notch and continues to work on that. 
Amit Chandra: And sir, in this quarter, what was the pledge income and the e-voting income if you can give? 
Nehal Vora: I'll ask Girish to do? 
Girish Amesara: Margin pledge income was INR6.19 crores. 
Amit Chandra: E-voting and e-CAS? 
Girish Amesara: e-CAS income was INR12.77 crores and e-voting income was INR22 crores. 
Moderator: We will take our next question from the line of Swarnabh Mukherjee from 360 ONE Capital. 
Swarnabh Mukherjee: Congratulations on a great set of numbers. My first question is on the IPO corporate action 
business. So yes, it's fairly understood that IPO income has been very strong this quarter. I just 
wanted some color from you that if I were to look at the corporate action part of the business 
this quarter, how has the growth been? Of course, I think the IPO portfolio-led income would 
have grown at a much faster pace.

But if you could give some indication on how the growth in the corporate action business has 
been in line with, say, how the number of companies getting listed incrementally over the year. 
If you can provide some color, that would be very helpful. That is the first question. 
Secondly, on the KRA revenue part, you mentioned that the volumes have kind of covered up 
for the pricing part. Two questions there. One, I wanted to understand that the search API-led 
pricing that you had mentioned last quarter, how is that faring? Has that also improved this 
quarter vis-a-vis last quarter, some details on that? 
And secondly, sir, the price that you have mentioned just now if you look to the previous 
participant. I just wanted to understand whether that is the rack rate or the blended price. You 
had mentioned, I think INR5 and INR28 for creation and fetch. So, if you can give some color, 
whether it is a rack rate or blended price? And if it is rack rate, then if you could please give 
some indication on the blended price? 
And third question, sir, in terms of other expenses, there is a jump on a sequential basis. I just 
wanted to understand how to related to that is that something related to business promotion? Or 
is this like a backing expense to revenue item like, say, inter-KRA, or e-AGM, e-voting income? 
Yes, these will be my questions and if you could provide the data keeping question in terms of 
what is the unlisted part in the annual issuer charges and processing fee for that. 
Nehal Vora: I'll ask Girish to answer the first and third question. And also, this follow-up question was that, 
unlisted. 
Girish Amesara: When we look at IPO corporate action income, it is a consolidated income for us. We internally 
do not monitor as to what would be corporate action revenue, what would be IPO-related revenue 
etc. Basically, it's a total revenue set for us, which keep on happening at our end, which is again 
largely based on the number of IPOs and the number of subscribers subscribed to that IPO. So, 
it's a commingled item, and we do not internally track as to what is corporate action-related 
revenue and what is IPO-related revenue. 
Having said that, your last question was on other admin expense, right? Other admin expense, 
largely, there are certain variable expenses like SMS alert and revenue expenses, which are 
directly linked with the operational activity that happens in the business. So, if there is a growth 
in that business activity, the operational expenditures tend to increase. That is the main reason 
for higher other admin expense compared to previous quarter. I hope I have answered that 
question. 
Nehal Vora: And on the second one, Sunil can answer. 
Sunil Alvares: The, the first question on the KRA rack rate and blended rate. The, the rates which I had indicated 
are the rack rates. On the blended rates, we do not discuss it in the public domain for obvious 
reasons. On the KRA side, the other expenses have increased primarily because the 
interoperability expenses have increased with the increase in fetch volumes. Point number two 
is we also do e-sign where you need to do Aadhaar-based eKYC first. So, there is a charge 
payable to UIDAI. With, with the higher number of e-signs done in this particular quarter, the 
amount payable to UIDAI has gone up.

And thirdly, we have also started doing Aadhaar-based eKYC separately. We, we have now 
started registering sub-KUAs for this facility, and we've seen that particular income also going 
up. We also need to pay UIDAI accordingly for the number of records, which we have processed 
on behalf of the sub-KUAs. 
And on the search API, the revenue as compared to the first quarter has come down primarily 
because it was earlier free and now it is chargeable. The intermediaries have started fine-tuning 
their system and the number of transactions has also come down. I hope that answers your 
question. 
Swarnabh Mukherjee: Yes, sir. Very clear. Sir, if you could also give the split on the unlisted revenue part. 
Girish Amesara: Sure. 
Nehal Vora: Girish. 
Girish Amesara: Sure, sir. I'll give. So unlisted revenue in terms of issuer fees is INR87 lakhs and application 
processing fees is INR2.2 crores. 
Moderator: We'll take our next question from the line of Madhukar Ladha from JPMorgan. 
Madhukar Ladha: Two quick ones. One on the IPO and corporate action revenue. You also earn money on KYC 
that you do in an IPO. What are the charges for that? So, per KYC, how much do you get? And 
I'm assuming that, that is booked in IPO and corporate action. 
And can you give a split between that, how much is the KYC revenue? That would be helpful. 
And second, can you give me the absolute rack rates? I think you did mention it earlier, but I 
missed it. Can you give me the absolute per the revised rate for creation and fetch once more? 
Nehal Vora: I'll ask Girish to answer the first and Sunil to answer the other. 
Girish Amesara: So, when you say KYC, what I've understood is it is the BO verification that we have to do when 
anyone applies for an application in an IPO. The charge for that is INR2 per application. With 
respect to the rack rate for creation, it is INR5 and for fetch, it is INR28. 
Madhukar Ladha: And sir, in the INR102 crores of IPO and corporate action, how much is the verification charge? 
Nehal Vora: We don't give that. It is typically a consolidated number. 
Girish Amesara: See, basically, Madhukar, what happens is that when any IPO comes out, depending upon the 
number of times it gets oversubscribed, value gets derived based on that. So, it would be very 
difficult to give a pinpointed answer that this IPO has yielded this revenue. So totally, it is a 
function of market with respect to how IPO is oversubscribed and then accordingly, you get the 
revenue. 
Moderator: Next question is from the line of Lalit Deo from Equirus Securities.

Lalit Deo: Sir, just one question on the KYC business. So, like one of our competitors has indicated that 
they have been onboarding brokers for newer KYC applications, and they have been able to add 
like 5 of the top 10 brokers. So just wanted to understand like how is the competitive intensity 
shaping up in this KYC segment? And yes, so that is my first question, sir. 
Nehal Vora: I'll ask Sunil to answer. 
Sunil Alvares: The problem is if he says that he has onboarded and if I say no, what will you actually take. So, 
these things happen and personally, I really cannot comment on this. But I think it will reflect in 
our numbers and in the financials what we have reported for this quarter. 
Moderator: Lalit, you're through with your question? 
Lalit Deo: Yes. 
Moderator: As there are no further questions, I would now like to hand the conference over to Mr. Nehal 
Vora for closing comments. Over to you. 
Nehal Vora: There is one question that's just come up. 
Moderator: It is from Sanketh Godha from Avendus Spark. 
Sanketh Godha: Sir, just 2 questions. One question is on you alluded in a couple of calls back that we don't have 
probably rights to give ISIN numbers for the unlisted companies. So just wanted to understand 
whether there has been any progress on that particular point so that our unlisted revenue sees a 
meaningful growth the way we have seen in the competition? 
And secondly, I just wanted to understand one more thing is that sir, pledge income typically 
looks a little lower given MTF book has grown so strong. So, it's largely flat on a sequential 
basis, INR6.2 crores. So just wanted to understand the strong growth in margin trade funding 
book is not benefiting us in growth in the pledging book. 
Nehal Vora: On the first one, it is going through the regulatory supervision, and it's in that process. So, I'd 
not like to comment it, but it is in process of ability. And on the second one, as the MTF book 
grows, we have multiple points on terms of where the revenue can grow. 
We don't have a 1:1 correlation. What we present is the overall income, which happens. But as 
we speak, the book of MTF is growing and these have been a significant growth which has 
happened on the CDSL side. I hope I'm able to answer that question. 
Sanketh Godha: Understood, sir. And last one data keeping. If you can give you an impairment cost in the 
quarter? And the second question, sir, is just from any major discount broker who is associated 
with CDSL, has incrementally started opening accounts with the other or we still enjoy the 
exclusive tie-up? I just want to understand from a business development point of view. 
Nehal Vora: So, the first one, I'll ask Girish to answer but before that, I'll answer the second one. One is we 
don't comment on any specific individual DPs. As I've said earlier, the important thing is to build

the right infrastructure and the value proposition, and the numbers speak for itself. So that is for 
you to take a call. I'll ask Girish to answer the first one. 
Girish Amesara: So Sanketh in terms of debtor’s provision, there is a reversal of INR1.77 crores. 
Sanketh Godha: INR1.77 crores. Okay, perfect, sir. 
Moderator: Next question is from the line of Pratik Shah, an Individual Shareholder. 
Pratik Shah: Firstly, congratulations for the set of numbers. Just wanted to understand from the insurance 
business side. As you know that CDSL has already tie-up and partnership with some of the 
insurance companies. So, if you can just give some color on how that business is shaping and 
how much revenue we have on in this quarter compared to the previous quarter or compared 
with the previous year? 
Nehal Vora: So, we continue to engage with the insurance companies. We have a new MD and CEO, who 
has joined there in terms of the experience, and he is kind of experienced in the industry. It's part 
of our continuing journey of ensuring people are strengthened in key positions. I'll ask the CFO 
to answer the second question, revenue. 
Girish Amesara: See, in insurance, we have earned a revenue of roughly INR2 crores in these 6 months. 
Pratik Shah: And maybe compared to what we have earned the previous quarter? 
Girish Amesara: In the 1st half of previous year, it was almost the same. 
Pratik Shah: Okay. Perfect. Also, just kind of a suggestion if we just start putting this number into our 
consolidated revenue side, just to understand how this business is shaping though its number is 
very small compared to the other segregate part of revenue, but just to understand how this is 
growing, so if you can put this number in the percentage. 
Nehal Vora: Yes, yes. Suggestion is taken. We will definitely look at it based on the framework and the 
practices getting followed by other companies also. But your suggestion is very welcome, and 
we shall definitely take it on and we shall look at it if it's feasible. 
Moderator: As there are no further questions, I would now like to hand the conference over to Mr. Nehal 
Vora for closing comments. Over to you. 
Nehal Vora: So, I would like to thank all the people who joined this investor call, continue to remain safe, 
and we continue to embark on our journey to ensuring CDSL continues to remain safe, secure. 
Thank you so much, and all the very best. 
Moderator: Thank you, members of the management. On behalf of HDFC Securities, that concludes this 
conference. Thank you all for joining us, and you may now disconnect your lines.
